title: Rigveda 4.54: To Savitri
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 4.54: To Savitri: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 4.54 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Savitri. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 4, the family book of Vāmadeva. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 313r-313v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 4.54.1-3 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 8, varga 5); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 313r
translation.original_text:
1abhū̍d de̱vaḥ sa̍vi̱tā vandyo̱ nu na̍ i̱dānī̱m ahna̍ upa̱vācyo̱ nṛbhi̍ḥ | vi yo ratnā̱ bhaja̍ti māna̱vebhya̱ḥ śreṣṭha̍ṁ no̱ atra̱ dravi̍ṇa̱ṁ yathā̱ dadha̍t ||
2de̱vebhyo̱ hi pra̍tha̱maṁ ya̱jñiye̍bhyo 'mṛta̱tvaṁ su̱vasi̍ bhā̱gam u̍tta̱mam | ād id dā̱māna̍ṁ savita̱r vy ū̍rṇuṣe 'nūcī̱nā jī̍vi̱tā mānu̍ṣebhyaḥ ||
3aci̍ttī̱ yac ca̍kṛ̱mā daivye̱ jane̍ dī̱nair dakṣai̱ḥ prabhū̍tī pūruṣa̱tvatā̍ | de̱veṣu̍ ca savita̱r mānu̍ṣeṣu ca̱ tvaṁ no̱ atra̍ suvatā̱d anā̍gasaḥ ||
translation.text:
1Now must we praise and honour Savitar the God: at this time of the day the men must call to him, Him who distributes wealth to Manu's progeny, that he may grant us here riches most excellent.
2For thou at first producest for the holy Gods the noblest of all portions, immor-tality: Thereafter as a gift to men, O Savitar, thou openest existence, life succeeding life.
3If we, men as we are, have sinned against the Gods through want of thought, in weakness, or through insolence, Absolve us from the guilt and make us free from sin, O Savitar, alike among both Gods and men.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 313r (numbered 122r by the scribe) (OPenn image 313, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 4.53.7 ‹-ṛtu-bhiḥ vardhatu kṣayam dadhātu›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 313v (numbered 122v by the scribe), begins in RV 4.54.4 ‹-dhārayiṣyati yat pṛthivyāḥ variman›. Verses 4.54.1-3 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 4.54.4-6 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 8, varga 5); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 313v
translation.original_text:
4na pra̱miye̍ savi̱tur daivya̍sya̱ tad yathā̱ viśva̱m bhuva̍naṁ dhārayi̱ṣyati̍ | yat pṛ̍thi̱vyā vari̍ma̱nn ā sva̍ṅgu̱rir varṣma̍n di̱vaḥ su̱vati̍ sa̱tyam a̍sya̱ tat ||
5indra̍jyeṣṭhān bṛ̱hadbhya̱ḥ parva̍tebhya̱ḥ kṣayā̍m̐ ebhyaḥ suvasi pa̱styā̍vataḥ | yathā̍-yathā pa̱taya̍nto viyemi̱ra e̱vaiva ta̍sthuḥ savitaḥ sa̱vāya̍ te ||
6ye te̱ trir aha̍n savitaḥ sa̱vāso̍ di̱ve-di̍ve̱ saubha̍gam āsu̱vanti̍ | indro̱ dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī sindhu̍r a̱dbhir ā̍di̱tyair no̱ adi̍ti̱ḥ śarma̍ yaṁsat ||
translation.text:
4None may impede that power of Savitar the God whereby he will maintain the universal world. What the fair-fingered God brings forth on earth's expanse or in the heightof heaven, that work of his stands sure.
5To lofty hills thou sendest those whom Indra leads, and givest fixed abodes with houses unto these. However they may fly and draw themselves apart, still, Savitar, they stand obeying thy behest.
6May the libations poured to thee thrice daily, day after day, O Savitar, bring us blessing. May Indra, Heaven, Earth, Sindhu with the Waters, Aditi with Âdityas, give us shelter.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 313v (numbered 122v by the scribe) (OPenn image 314, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 4.54.4 ‹-dhārayiṣyati yat pṛthivyāḥ variman›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 314r (numbered 123r by the scribe), begins in RV 4.55.2 ‹-ucchān vi-yotāraḥ amūrāḥ vi-dhātāraḥ›. Verses 4.54.4-6 end on this page; 4.54.4 begins on fol. 313r (numbered 122r by the scribe).
